The ground‑fault trips are most likely caused by the long unshielded cable picking up stray currents that the VFD interprets as a fault. The most effective fix is to replace the cable with a properly shielded type and terminate the shield to ground at the drive (source) end only, preventing induced noise from reaching the VFD’s ground‑fault detector.  

1. De‑energize and lock‑out the VFD, verify zero voltage.  
2. Remove the existing 150 ft unshielded cable.  
3. Install a shielded power cable of the same current rating; connect the shield to the drive chassis ground only at the drive end (leave it floating at the motor end).  
4. Re‑energize and confirm the VFD no longer trips on ground fault.  

(Other options either don’t address the source of the fault or could compromise protection.)
